angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 292,194 km at 46.25 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 21.6228 +/- 0.0157 mas (same row, RUWE 1.35): 46.25 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.42 +/- 0.013 solar radii from Murgas et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-674 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...653A..60M/abstract): 292,194 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.42 +/- 0.01 solar masses from Murgas et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-674 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...653A..60M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3514 +/- 57 K from Murgas et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-674 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...653A..60M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Murgas et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-674 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...653A..60M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-674.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.815, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
